title: Does net1's stated uncertainty help where information has value? Spread rules on the info and rise families
description: A net2 on the means of net1's beliefs (A2) has done as well as one on the full beliefs (A3), but on links the flow keeps busy: the fixed rule alone keeps 96% of validation steps on a fully busy link, where net1's capacity belief is narrow (median log2 sd 0.14) and its spread has nothing to say. Off a busy link the spread widens 3 to 6 times, stays honest (90% coverage 0.95 to 0.98) and tracks the error (correlation 0.82; local analysis of exp-net2-competitor-info-177). Two new families (experiments/heldout.py) put the flow where it cannot see the capacity: info (a Cubic or BBRv1 flow leaving at 10 s; UDP at half the mean capacity on 2 s, off 2 s; Cubic on 3 s, off 3 s) and rise (alone, capacity alternating between half and twice its first level every 2 s). The A3 arms are the fixed rule with its window target raised by k times net1's spread of log2 capacity past s0 (train/models.py SpreadTarget; k = 0 is the rule): k 1 at s0 0.2, k 2 at 0.4, and k 1 at 0.2 lifted only by 1 - P(copies) from net1's traffic head, since net1's spread is also wide on any shared link (0.34 to 0.42 with copies or a stock flow). The A2 arms probe on means alone: the target raised by k times how idle net1 believes the link is, 1 minus its mean busy fraction past 0.05 (IdleTarget), k 1 and 2. A3 beating the best A2 arm where information has value is what would show the spread's worth. Beside net1 v6's fixed rule (A2), r18e05 and BBRv3, on every validation family, as copies and on both new families, campaign seed 21. versus-rule-v6.md has each arm minus the rule per campaign and condition. Validation only.
prepare: N="$IN/v6/net1-v6-s0/net1.pt"; H="$IN/head/traffic_head.pt"; (cd "$IN/veto" && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS); (cd "$IN/head" && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS); uv run python experiments/rule_export.py "$OUT/r02" "$N" --u 0.25 --spread 1 --s0 0.2 --idle 1 2; uv run python experiments/rule_export.py "$OUT/r04" "$N" --u 0.25 --spread 2 --s0 0.4; uv run python experiments/rule_export.py "$OUT/rh" "$N" --u 0.25 --spread 1 --s0 0.2 --traffic "$H"; P=(--policy "rule-v6=$OUT/r02/rule-u0.25.onnx" --policy "spread1=$OUT/r02/rule-u0.25-spread1.onnx" --policy "spread2-s04=$OUT/r04/rule-u0.25-spread2.onnx" --policy "spread1-head=$OUT/rh/rule-u0.25-spread1-head.onnx" --policy "idle1=$OUT/r02/rule-u0.25-idle1.onnx" --policy "idle2=$OUT/r02/rule-u0.25-idle2.onnx" --policy "ppo-r18e05-s0=$IN/veto/ppo-r18e05-s0.onnx"); RULE_EVAL_FAMILIES="training:20 training:60 new:20 deep-long:20 cubic-first:60 info:30 rise:30" experiments/rule_eval.sh "$OUT" val 21 21 bbr3 "${P[@]}"; uv run python experiments/copies.py "$OUT/copies" --split val --duration-ms 30000 --seed 21 --n 2 4 --stock bbr3 "${P[@]}"; mv "$OUT/copies/c-copies-30s" "$OUT/"; jq -s add "$OUT/aliases.json" "$OUT/copies/aliases.json" > "$OUT/a.json"; mv "$OUT/a.json" "$OUT/aliases.json"
run: for c in "$OUT"/c-*; do uv run expliccit campaign run "$c" --shard "$SHARD/$SHARDS" --build "$UML" --workers "$WORKERS" --tables steps; done; uv run python experiments/slim_steps.py "$OUT"
collect: uv run python experiments/rule_report.py "$OUT" --apart copies-30s info-30 rise-30 && mv "$OUT/summary.md" "$OUT/against-bbr3.md" && uv run python experiments/versus_rule.py "$OUT" rule-v6 && cp "$OUT/versus-rule-v6.md" "$OUT/summary.md"
